## About This Repository

Welcome to the **LeetCode Solutions** repository. Here you will find daily **LeetCode solutions in C++**, each with analysis, learnings, implementation, and approaches.

Use this repository to prepare for coding interviews, build strong problem-solving skills, and develop algorithmic thinking. It is my attempt to make the coding experience easier for you, so you can learn what to do and why. I am always here to assist you.

It also serves as a log of my own journey: tracking progress and consistency, documenting analysis, approaches, and learnings, reinforcing my understanding of data structures and algorithms (DSA), and practicing coding regularly, while helping others do the same.

## What You Get With Every Solution

Every problem is documented with the same structure (see [`template.md`](template.md)).

## LeetCode Solutions by Topic

Solutions are grouped by topic and follow the **NeetCode 250** roadmap, a curated list that covers the core data structures and algorithms asked in coding interviews.

<p align="center">

## Repository Structure

Every problem lives in its own folder, grouped by topic. Names such as `topic_name` and `problem_name` are placeholders for the real names.

```text
leetcode-solutions/
├── topic_name/                   # main topic folder
│   ├── problem_name/             # main problem folder
│   │   ├── problem_name.ext      # solution code
│   │   └── problem_name.md       # intuition, approach, complexity analysis
│   └── ...
├── ...
├── template.md                   # documentation template for new solutions
└── README.md
```

Before you submit, make sure that:

- Your code passes all the test cases on LeetCode for the problem it solves.
- Your write-up follows `template.md`.
- It includes the approach, time and space complexity analysis, learnings, and implementation.

I write the solutions in C++, but contributions in other languages are just as welcome, whether that is Python, Java, JavaScript, or any other language. If you would like to add a solution in a language that is not here yet, please go ahead.

Thank you for helping make these solutions accessible and valuable to the community!

## Frequently Asked Questions

<details>
<summary><b>Where can I find LeetCode solutions in C++ with explanations?</b></summary>

<br>

Right here. Every solution includes C++ code, intuition, approach, time and space complexity analysis, and notes. Browse them in the [solutions by topic](#solutions).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Is this repository beginner friendly?</b></summary>

<br>

Yes. The code is written to be clear and readable, and every solution explains the intuition and approach step by step. The repository follows the NeetCode 250 list, which NeetCode describes as its most beginner-friendly list.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>What is the NeetCode 250 list?</b></summary>

<br>

NeetCode 250 is a curated problem list made by NeetCode. It is the NeetCode 150 list plus 100 more problems, organized into 18 topics from Arrays &amp; Hashing to Bit Manipulation. This repository currently follows it.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>How do I prepare for coding interviews with LeetCode?</b></summary>

<br>

Follow a structured list such as NeetCode 250 instead of picking problems at random. Work through it topic by topic, attempt every problem yourself before reading a solution, review the time and space complexity, and revisit problems regularly to reinforce the pattern.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>How often is this repository updated?</b></summary>

<br>

I try to solve problems on a daily basis and update the repository and documentation on a daily or weekly schedule. Star the repository to keep up with progress.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>How do I find today's problem or the latest solution?</b></summary>

<br>

Use the **Today's Problem** button at the top, which opens the LeetCode problem list where the daily challenge is shown, and the **Recently Solved** button for the newest solutions.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Are there solutions in languages other than C++?</b></summary>

<br>

Not yet. I write the solutions in C++, but contributions in other languages are very welcome. If you would like to add one, see [Contributing](#contributing).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Can I use or copy the code?</b></summary>

<br>

You are free to read, use, and adapt the code, analysis, learnings, implementations, and approaches. Just give credit. Please attempt the problems yourself first and avoid copy-pasting.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Is there a more optimal solution?</b></summary>

<br>

Possibly. These solutions reflect my approach and understanding, and many problems have more than one valid approach. If you have a better solution, please see [Contributing](#contributing).

</details>

## Disclaimer

These solutions represent my approach and understanding, based on my own experience while solving the problems. They are intended for learning and reference purposes.

There may be more optimal or more efficient ways to solve these problems, which is why contributions are welcome.

Attempt each problem yourself before looking at any solution, and avoid copy-pasting. Learning comes from hard work and struggle.

## License

You are free to read, use, and adapt the code, analysis, learnings, implementations, and approaches. Just don't forget to give credit.
